note: The input-controlled HTTP request buffer is passed to the real header parser after the request line is accepted.
Each malformed header line is located by scanning from the current input pointer toward buffer_end.
A carriage return not followed by a real line ending advances p two bytes, potentially beyond the received buffer.
The safety obligation is that p must remain below buffer_end before the next scan; without this bound the following length calculation underflows.
When p is past buffer_end, buffer_end - p becomes negative and is cast to a huge size_t, making memchr read out of bounds.
